findings.location: section 3 'Schedule changes', wizard-steps component, id s3-wizard
findings.evidence: DOM order is div id=s3-step3 style="order:3" 'Confirm your order', then id=s3-step2 style="order:2" 'Enter payment details', then id=s3-step1 style="order:1" 'Choose a plan'. The CSS order values (3, 2, 1) reverse this so the intended visual sequence is Choose a plan, Enter payment details, Confirm your order.
findings.violation: The wizard-steps component's DOM order is the reverse of the sequence its own CSS order values establish, so a reader whose assistive technology linearizes by DOM order hears the confirm-and-pay step before hearing what is being chosen or paid for, reversing the actual decision sequence.
findings.fix: Reorder the three step div elements in the DOM to match the intended sequence (Choose a plan, Enter payment details, Confirm your order) instead of relying on the CSS order property to establish that sequence visually.

findings.location: section 3 'Schedule changes', custom control div, id s3-customcontrol
findings.evidence: , no role, no aria-label or aria-labelledby, no tabindex attribute anywhere on the div.
findings.violation: The custom control div carries no role, no programmatically determinable accessible name, and no keyboard handler; its only content is an icon marked decorative (alt=""), so assistive technology cannot detect that this control exists at all, let alone that activating it deletes something.
findings.fix: Replace the div with a native button element carrying the icon and a visible or aria-label accessible name (for example "Delete"), or add role="button", an aria-label, and a tabindex="0" with keyboard activation handling to the existing div.

findings.location: page level, header nav, id nav
findings.evidence:
Plan a tripService alerts
is the only navigation mechanism in the document; no search form, sitemap link, or breadcrumb trail appears anywhere, and the footer carries only Privacy policy and Terms of service utility links.
findings.violation: The page relies solely on its primary navigation menu, with no second independent mechanism such as a site search or breadcrumb trail, and the page is not one step in a linear process, so a reader who lands here directly has exactly one way to find any related page.
findings.fix: Add a second, independent way to locate this page and related pages, such as a site search form or a breadcrumb trail reflecting this page's place in the site, distinct from the primary nav menu.

findings.evidence: <label for="phone" id="s3-form-phone-label" style="color:#cc0000">Phone number</label> is the only one of the form's four labels (Route, Email address, Phone number, Promo code) carrying any color styling, with no asterisk, no required text, and no aria-required attribute on the phone input.
findings.violation: The Phone number label is distinguished from the form's other labels only by red text color, with no accompanying text, icon, or aria-required attribute carrying the same meaning, so a color-blind reader cannot tell why this field is singled out.
findings.fix: Add a non-color signal alongside the color, such as a visible asterisk or the word required in the label text, or set aria-required="true" on the phone input.

findings.evidence:
Accessibility improvements

introduces a paragraph about requesting a fare adjustment through the mobile app and a paragraph about checking real-time arrivals by phone; neither paragraph describes an accessibility improvement.
findings.violation: The heading Accessibility improvements misdescribes the section's content, which is mainly about fare-adjustment requests and phone-based arrival information rather than accessibility, so a reader scanning headings for accessibility-specific content is misled by this one.
findings.fix: Rename the heading to describe the section's actual content, for example Rider services, or move the fare-adjustment and real-time-arrival paragraphs elsewhere and keep only accessibility-related content under this heading.

findings.location: section 3 form, promo code field and its error text, id s3-form-promo-error
findings.violation: The promo code field's error text reads only Error, which signals that something is wrong but names neither the specific problem nor what to do about it.
findings.fix: Replace the error text with a message naming the specific problem, for example Promo code not recognized. Check the code and try again.
